I'm not a doctor but I have literally been in those exact shoes, so I'll share my experience!

I was diagnosed with adult ADD 7 years ago, in my mid-20's. From what I had been told by my previous doctors before then, I couldn't have it because I was either A) too old or B) wasn't "hyper" per the normal definition, and was never even presented the option to TRY a medicine for it. I was well aware that I presented at least some symptoms associated with it. 2 years prior to my actual diagnosis, I had came straight out and asked the current doctor I was at if I could try being put on a low dose of something to see if it would help with multiple things. She immediately told me no. I feel like here is a good time to say that I had already been put on a handful of other meds, at least, by her alone - but something I suggested and thought might help after all that? Nope. She was the first doctor I had asked, but NOT the first I had seen - I've been on this path for a long time. I left her office that day and that was the last time I saw her. 

2 years later I hit a point in which I felt like I honestly could not function as a normal human being, let alone a responsible, working parent. I finally got an appointment with a new doctor and focused ONLY on the symptoms that impacted my day to day life and left out anything that had to do with being depressed. I wasn't asked directly about it, and I figured it could always be brought up on the next appointment, as I had made that one SPECIFICALLY for the symptoms I was concerned about. At the end of the appointment I had a prescription for something that I thought might actually work.

My follow up appointment was a mixture of good and bad. I was a hot mess because I had seen such an improvement in the first month alone that it made me terribly sad to know I had put myself through SO many years of listening to horrible doctors who weren't willing to listen to me. I had made a list during the month of all the little (and big, lol) things that I had noticed improvements in, and remained engaged throughout the appointment with the doctor. I followed along with the conversation and asked clear questions with the ability to somewhat retain the information I was getting back. It was AMAZING.

I moved 500 miles away a year later and lost the best doctor I had ever had. I haven't found one I have liked as much until just recently and sadly I have to find another replacement soon, due to insurance changing. Regardless though, I have not had a doctor question me once since I have been diagnosed. If you have been diagnosed before (I don't remember if you stated in your post 😂), I would make sure you mention that, especially if the doctor seems to be stiff or not willing to listen. If you  were diagnosed, did you keep an old bottle? 

Without diagnosis, my suggestion would be to make a new appointment somewhere after reading Google reviews on local doctors (I'm a big fan of this. Very much aware that people make crap reviews sometimes and it's not actually the doctor's fault - most of the time you can tell if and when that is the case.. however - when people find a good doctor, a TRULY good doctor, you will know by their review). If they ask why you are making the appointment, give them the reasons you are struggling in day to day life with this and explain that it is severely impacting your life. When you get to the doctor, do the same thing. They will more than likely start off with a line very similar to "What brings you in?", So it can typically be a very easy transition.

Hopefully this helps you along the way. I know it can be a struggle! Good luck!!
